# Welcome {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```{=html}
<div class="abstract-section">
  <div class="abstract-content">
    <p>Agentic machine learning systems represent a fundamental shift in computing infrastructure: the transition from stateless, request-scoped token generation to stateful, autonomous trajectory execution. When a foundation model is given memory, tools, and a delegated goal, the system ceases to be an oracle and becomes an actor.</p>
    <p>This volume establishes the systems engineering foundations of agentic AI, governed by the <strong>H·S·A Triad (Horizon, State, Authority)</strong> and the <strong>Invariant Closure Principle</strong>. The treatment covers four core areas: foundations of trajectories and state graphs, the AI-native memory hierarchy (attention working sets, Radix prefix caching, durable episodic stores), the agent–world boundary (typed contracts, microVM sandboxes, distributed Sagas), and trajectory measurement and fleet economics.</p>
  </div>
```

## What You Will Learn {.unnumbered}

The book progresses through four thematic parts:

- **Part I: The Trajectory as the Unit of Work**—From stateless requests to managed trajectories, formalizing Agent Control Blocks (ACB), state DAGs, scheduling, and compounding error mathematics ($P_{\text{success}} \le p^N$).
- **Part II: The AI-Native Memory & Context Hierarchy**—Context working set management, token LRU eviction, Radix tree KV prefix caching, scratchpad transaction isolation, and durable episodic stores with temporal decay.
- **Part III: The Agent–World Boundary**—Model Context Protocol (MCP) typed schema contracts, microVM sandboxing (Firecracker / Wasm), information flow control, and distributed Sagas with deterministic compensating rollbacks.
- **Part IV: Measurement, Verification & Fleet Economics**—Trajectory benchmarks (SWE-bench, GAIA, MLPerf Agents), non-deterministic replay debugging, OpenTelemetry distributed tracing, and the macro-economics of useful work per dollar and joule.

## Prerequisites {.unnumbered}

This book assumes:

- **Systems & Programming Proficiency** in Python and systems concepts (concurrency, caching, state machines, and networking).
- **Machine Learning Foundations** at the level of Volume I (*Single-Node Systems*) and Volume II (*Distributed Scale*).

:::
